previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis and a J-tube presented with acute nausea and vomiting after eating cereal with milk, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She was admitted for symptom management and received IV fluids and anti-nausea medications. Her white blood cell count was initially elevated but normalized during the stay, attributed to a stress response. A J-tube study confirmed the tube was patent and correctly positioned. Her TSH was found to be elevated at 4.3, prompting an increase in levothyroxine dose from 100 to 125 mcg daily. She tolerated advancement to a regular diet and was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up on thyroid function and discuss potential intermittent J-tube feeding with her GI specialist.
